data.narrative:
Foundry Robotics, a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Adarsh Kulkarni, has raised $19M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a competitive universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though the narrow peer set at identical stage limits the strength of cross-sectional benchmarking.

Stage-progression methodology was the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($19M) as a value proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from Seed to the next institutional round, this method implies a valuation of $48M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics sector narrowly defined; the broader sector peer set of 10 firms lacks sufficient density at Foundry's stage to support robust median benchmarking without introducing material bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $40M to $55M, with a median point estimate of $48M. This range reflects uncertainty around the appropriate stage-progression multiple and the absence of tight peer validation. Key risks to valuation include the company's actual unit economics relative to more mature robotics platforms, path to revenue materiality, and execution against current capital efficiency. Additional disclosure of revenue traction or capital deployment efficiency would significantly narrow this range.
